title: Counted length is a measure on the knot's spaces
claim: Counted length is a measure on the knot's spaces. Let H be a knot's space (a connected cubic system on which not-all-equal fails) and A(H) its amplitude, half the number of colourings of H minus a line, which is the same for every line (THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE). (1) Across every nontrivial 2- or 3-edge cut, each side has the same number a(X) of colourings for every channel assignment it accepts: by complement symmetry on two-state sides, and by the point lemma with the one amplitude on the six-state line side. (2) The two sides multiply to the whole: a(X) a(X-bar) = A(H), since the atom twist of a cut edge has 2 a(X) a(X-bar) colourings and also 2 A(H). So counted length, l(X) = log a(X), is additive over every cut and over the whole decomposition into parts: a measure. (3) It is worth log 5 per Fano block, which is one handle where THREEFOLD-SURFACES applies, plus the logarithm of the glue's tree-trinity number (log 2 in the twisted cube). Along a route of m Fano units it is m log 5, which no relation sees (relations keep m mod 2). (4) In rings of units cut from different knot's spaces, every unit is a negation, the ring fails exactly when the number of units is odd, and the count is the product of the units' amplitudes, so the relation and the count vary independently: the relation counts parts, the count counts handles and glue. (5) It is unchanged by transposition, which exchanges knot sides and hub sides, and by isomorphism, but not by replacing a part with a relationally equal one. Reading: a law-intrinsic measure on the routes of the declared substrate, which supplies canonical weights where earlier route values needed chosen ones; since these routes are not native paths, it is counted length, not a native extended distance.
failure_conditions: A line of a knot's space at which the amplitude differs.
A side of a nontrivial 2- or 3-edge cut whose count differs between two accepted channel assignments.
A cut whose two side counts do not multiply to the amplitude.
A ring of units whose failure or count disagrees with the parity of its units or the product of their amplitudes.
A knot's space whose transpose has a different amplitude.
foundation_claim_scope: Counts of colourings on declared finite systems; no native extended distance is constructed.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-01.
validation.status: checked: the amplitude at every line of ten knot's spaces; uniform side counts and their product at every nontrivial 2- and 3-edge cut; arcs of cycles; rings of units cut from three different spaces; transposes; no human or external review
validation.novelty: The point lemma, the one amplitude, the factorization over tight cuts and five per handle are ours (THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE, THREEFOLD-SURFACES); the measure statement over both kinds of cut, the rings and the reading are new here.
